prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what matters most to you (price, speed, workmanship, color help, warranty). I can’t pick a single company for you, but I can help you find the best one for your job. A quick plan:

1) Narrow your needs
- Home or business? How many rooms/sq ft? Do you need ceilings, trim, doors, priming, drywall repair, wallpaper removal, or color consultation? Desired start date and budget?

2) Where to search
- Check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi (Angi.com), Houzz, and the BBB for St. Louis-area painters. Ask neighbors or local Facebook/Nextdoor groups for recent referrals.

3) What to require from any candidate
- Proof of insurance (liability + workers’ comp)
- Local business license (if required)
- Written estimate with scope, materials/brands, prep work, number of coats, start and finish dates, cleanup, and payment terms
- Written warranty or guarantee
- References and photos of recent jobs

4) Questions to ask each painter
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?
- How many coats and what paint brand/line do you use?
- How do you handle prep (sanding, caulking, priming, patching)?
- Who will do the work—employees or subcontractors?
- Can you provide references from recent interior jobs in St. Louis?
- What’s your timeline and estimated completion date?
- What is your warranty on labor and workmanship?
- How do you protect floors/furniture and handle cleanup?

5) How to compare bids
- Compare apples-to-apples: same scope, same brands/number of coats, same prep and cleanup. The lowest price isn’t always best—look at references, photos, and warranty.
- Get at least three written bids.

6) Red flags
- Large upfront cash deposit required
- No proof of insurance
- No written contract or vague scope
- Poor or no references and no portfolio

If you want, tell me:
- whether this is residential or commercial,
- number of rooms/square feet and what surfaces need painting,
- any timing or budget constraints,

and I’ll give a tailored shortlist of what to ask contractors, a template message/email to send to painters, and help you evaluate up to three bids.
